findings.title: Upgraded realms never receive the new Clients resource type and scopes
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already non-null. A realm that had FGAP V2 enabled before this change already has that client, but its resource server only contains the Users resource/scopes; after upgrading, the 'Clients' resource and the configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite scopes are never created. As a result, creating a client permission fails in getScope() with ModelValidationException("Scope [configure] does not exist."), getOrCreateResource() for a client throws ModelException("No scopes found."), and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission() dereferences the null Resource returned by getResourceTypeResource() when calling policyStore.findByResource(server, null). init() must reconcile and add missing resource types/scopes instead of returning when the client exists.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission cannot find per-client resources
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission() iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). However, the per-client resources built by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() are created via resourceStore.create(...) and never get their type set to 'Clients' (only the 'all-clients' resource created in init() has that type and its name is 'Clients'). Consequently per-client grants are never returned; at best the single all-clients resource is evaluated and its name 'Clients' (not a client id) is added to the result. Any caller that uses this method to filter/return the clients an admin can act on receives wrong data. The fix is either to set the resource type when creating per-client resources, or to iterate the actual client resources and evaluate each.

findings.title: V2 client role-mapping checks ignore the manage-clients realm role and manage scope
findings.body: canMapRoles(), canMapCompositeRoles() and canMapClientScopeRoles() only evaluate the fine-grained MAP_ROLES / MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permissions. Unlike every other method in this class (canManage, canManageClientScopes, canView, canConfigure), they never check root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) nor canManage(client). An administrator holding only the built-in manage-clients role (the normal case, no fine-grained permissions) will therefore be denied adding/removing client roles and composites once V2 is enabled, which is a functional regression versus V1 and is inconsistent with the manage-implies-configure/view behavior implemented in this same class. These methods must also honor the built-in role and/or the manage scope.

findings.title: UnsupportedOperationException thrown from authorization paths that are actually invoked
findings.body: setPermissionsEnabled()/isPermissionsEnabled() and canExchangeTo() throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning false/no-op. These are reachable: AdminPermissions.registerListener() calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on ClientRemovedEvent (and roles()/groups() equivalents) whenever Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled; since V1 is enabled by default and can be on together with V2, deleting a client/role/group in a V2 realm will raise UnsupportedOperationException and abort the deletion. Conversely, when only V2 is enabled the listener is skipped entirely, so no cleanup of the deleted entity's resource/policies occurs. canExchangeTo() is invoked by the token-exchange authorization flow and will surface as HTTP 500 rather than a proper denial. These methods should return false/no-op (or be implemented), and the listener guard/cleanup should handle V2.
